# Setup troubleshooting

**English** · [Português](pt/TROUBLESHOOTING.md)

Every setup error has a **code** (for example, `E-NET-01`). The setup shows the code, the cause and what to do. This is the full catalog, by operating system.

## Before anything else

- Run the setup again: steps already done are skipped.
- Check only, without installing: `bash ~/.workshop-claude/setup-mac.sh --check` (Mac) or `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$env:USERPROFILE\.workshop-claude\setup-windows.ps1" -Check` (Windows).
- Diagnosis with Claude's help: `bash ~/.workshop-claude/setup-mac.sh --doctor` (Mac) or `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$env:USERPROFILE\.workshop-claude\setup-windows.ps1" -Doctor` (Windows).
- The full log, without secrets, is in `~/.workshop-claude/setup.log`. The summary is in `~/.workshop-claude/summary.txt`.
- Never send your API key to anyone. The setup never asks for it or shows it.

## macOS

<a id="mac-e-setup-01"></a>

### E-SETUP-01 · This step is not done yet

- **Why:** The setup has not installed this on this computer yet, or the install stopped halfway.
- **What to do:**
  - Run the full setup, without --check. Steps already done are skipped.

Command (macOS):

```
curl -fsSL https://github.com/cx-guilherme-pinto/workshop-claude/releases/download/v1.1.0-rc.1/setup-mac.sh | bash
```

<a id="mac-e-net-01"></a>

### E-NET-01 · A required domain is blocked

- **Why:** The network does not let you reach one or more domains that the workshop needs. This is usually a company firewall or filter.
- **What to do:**
  - Ask your IT team to allow the domains listed in docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md (section "Required domains").
  - Or use another network (for example, your phone's hotspot) and run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
curl -sSL -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{url_effective}\n' https://api.anthropic.com
```

<a id="mac-e-net-02"></a>

### E-NET-02 · The server name does not resolve (DNS)

- **Why:** The computer can't translate the domain name into an address. The network may require a VPN, or DNS is failing.
- **What to do:**
  - Connect to the company VPN if you use one, or disconnect it if it is blocking.
  - Try another network and run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
dscacheutil -q host -a name api.anthropic.com
```

<a id="mac-e-net-03"></a>

### E-NET-03 · The proxy does not answer or refuses the request

- **Why:** Your terminal sends the traffic through a proxy (HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY or the system proxy). That proxy does not answer, its name does not resolve, or it refused the request (for example, error 407: it asks for a username and password). A proxy left over from the office network or from an old VPN causes this.
- **What to do:**
  - If you are not on the office network or VPN, remove the proxy from this terminal (first command below) and delete the line that sets it in ~/.zshrc or ~/.zprofile. If it is the system proxy, turn it off in System Settings > Network > Details > Proxies. Then run the setup again.
  - On Windows, the second command removes the proxy from your user environment variables, and the system proxy is in Settings > Network & internet > Proxy.
  - If the company network needs the proxy, connect the VPN, or set the right proxy for this session and run the setup again.
  - If the proxy asks for a username and password (error 407), ask IT for a proxy without authentication or an exception for the workshop domains.
  - On Windows, if even the first command of the setup gets error 407, run it with the last command: it sends your Windows login to the proxy.

Commands (macOS):

```
unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy
grep -n -i proxy ~/.zshrc ~/.zprofile ~/.bash_profile
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.company:8080
export NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1
```

<a id="mac-e-net-04"></a>

### E-NET-04 · Your company intercepts HTTPS traffic (its own certificate)

- **Why:** A site the setup needs (api.anthropic.com, github.com or pypi.org) shows a certificate that does not come from a public authority: the company network opens the traffic and encrypts it again. The setup exports the company certificates from the system to ~/.workshop-claude/ca-company.pem, adds your ~/.workshop-claude/ca.pem if you have one, and configures Claude Code to use them and uv to use the system certificates.
- **What to do:**
  - Usually you don't need to do anything: the setup already set NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS and UV_SYSTEM_CERTS.
  - If the final test or the Agent Memory app still fails with a certificate error, ask IT for the company root certificate in PEM format and save it as ~/.workshop-claude/ca.pem (the setup never overwrites that file). Then run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
ls -l ~/.workshop-claude/ca.pem ~/.workshop-claude/ca-company.pem
```

<a id="mac-e-net-05"></a>

### E-NET-05 · No connection to the Anthropic API

- **Why:** Claude Code can't talk to api.anthropic.com. Without this there is no workshop, and Claude can't help you diagnose the problem either.
- **What to do:**
  - Check that you can open https://api.anthropic.com in the browser (a JSON error page means you can reach it).
  - If your network needs a proxy, set HTTPS_PROXY before you run the setup. If a proxy is already set, see E-NET-03 and E-NET-08.
  - Ask IT to allow api.anthropic.com, claude.ai and platform.claude.com.

Command (macOS):

```
curl -sv https://api.anthropic.com -o /dev/null
```

<a id="mac-e-net-06"></a>

### E-NET-06 · Proxy with NTLM or Kerberos authentication only

- **Why:** Claude Code and Node can't authenticate to NTLM or Kerberos proxies. This type of proxy is not supported.
- **What to do:**
  - Ask IT for a proxy exception for the workshop domains.
  - Or use another network (your phone's hotspot) during the workshop.

<a id="mac-e-net-07"></a>

### E-NET-07 · The download failed

- **Why:** A file was not downloaded, or it arrived incomplete (the transfer stopped in the middle). This is usually a short network failure or a crowded WiFi.
- **What to do:**
  - Run the setup again. Steps already done are skipped.
  - If it always fails on the same file, try another network (for example, your phone's hotspot) and check the proxy (codes E-NET-01 and E-NET-03).

Command (macOS):

```
curl -fsSL https://github.com/cx-guilherme-pinto/workshop-claude/releases/download/v1.1.0-rc.1/setup-mac.sh | bash
```

<a id="mac-e-net-08"></a>

### E-NET-08 · Claude Code is set to use a proxy that does not answer on this network

- **Why:** The "env" block of ~/.claude/settings.json has HTTPS_PROXY, and Claude Code uses it even when your terminal has no proxy. That proxy does not answer here. It is usually a proxy the setup saved on another network (for example, the office proxy).
- **What to do:**
  - Run the setup again on this network: it removes or updates the proxy it saved.
  - If you added this proxy yourself, delete the HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY lines from the "env" block of ~/.claude/settings.json.
  - Back on the office network, run the setup again to put the proxy back.

Commands (macOS):

```
curl -fsSL https://github.com/cx-guilherme-pinto/workshop-claude/releases/download/v1.1.0-rc.1/setup-mac.sh | bash
grep -n -i proxy ~/.claude/settings.json
```

<a id="mac-e-net-09"></a>

### E-NET-09 · A certificate variable points to a missing or wrong file

- **Why:** SSL_CERT_FILE, CURL_CA_BUNDLE, GIT_SSL_CAINFO, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or SSL_CERT_DIR (shown in brackets), or a cacert line in ~/.curlrc, points to a certificate file that does not exist or does not have the right certificates. It is often left over from an old Homebrew, Anaconda or Zscaler install. curl then fails on every site with "curl: (77) error setting certificate verify locations", and uv fails with "invalid peer certificate". The setup ignores the variable in its own commands, but your terminal still has it.
- **What to do:**
  - If the install command itself stops with curl: (77), run the first command below in the same terminal and paste the install command again.
  - Find the export in your shell profile with the second command, delete that line (or point it to the right file) and open a new terminal.

Commands (macOS):

```
unset SSL_CERT_FILE CURL_CA_BUNDLE GIT_SSL_CAINFO NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE SSL_CERT_DIR
grep -nE 'SSL_CERT|CA_BUNDLE|CAINFO|EXTRA_CA_CERTS|cacert' ~/.zshrc ~/.zprofile ~/.zshenv ~/.bash_profile ~/.profile ~/.curlrc 2>/dev/null
```

<a id="mac-e-net-10"></a>

### E-NET-10 · uv doesn't trust your company's certificate

- **Why:** Downloading the app's Python (github.com) or its packages (pypi.org) failed with a certificate error, even with the system certificates (UV_SYSTEM_CERTS) and with ~/.workshop-claude/ca.pem if you have one. Your company's root certificate is not among them.
- **What to do:**
  - Ask IT for the company root certificate in PEM format and save it as ~/.workshop-claude/ca.pem. The setup never overwrites that file.
  - Then run the setup again: it gives that certificate to uv. The commands below do the same by hand. The app is optional: the skills work without it.

Commands (macOS):

```
cat /etc/ssl/cert.pem ~/.workshop-claude/ca.pem > ~/.workshop-claude/ca-bundle-uv.pem
SSL_CERT_FILE=~/.workshop-claude/ca-bundle-uv.pem uv python install 3.12
```

<a id="mac-e-so-03"></a>

### E-SO-03 · Your home folder is in OneDrive

- **Why:** Your home folder, or the folder of the workshop projects, is synced by OneDrive. Syncing can lock files while the agents are working.
- **What to do:**
  - During the workshop, pause OneDrive syncing (OneDrive icon > Pause syncing).
  - The projects are in ~/workshop-claude. If that folder is inside OneDrive, move it out.

<a id="mac-e-so-04"></a>

### E-SO-04 · Old macOS

- **Why:** Claude Code needs macOS 13 or newer.
- **What to do:**
  - Update macOS in System Settings > General > Software Update.

Command (macOS):

```
sw_vers
```

<a id="mac-e-so-06"></a>

### E-SO-06 · Low disk space

- **Why:** There are less than 3 GB free in your home folder. The tools and the projects need about 2 GB.
- **What to do:**
  - Free up space (for example, empty the Downloads folder) and run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
df -h ~
```

<a id="mac-e-so-09"></a>

### E-SO-09 · The temporary folder variable points to a folder that cannot be used

- **Why:** TMPDIR (on Windows, TEMP or TMP), shown in brackets, points to a folder that does not exist or cannot be written, often an export copied from another computer. The setup used another temporary folder, but other programs in your terminal (Claude Code, uv, npm) may fail.
- **What to do:**
  - Find the export with the first command and delete it (macOS sets TMPDIR by itself), then open a new terminal.

Commands (macOS):

```
grep -n TMPDIR ~/.zshrc ~/.zprofile ~/.zshenv ~/.bash_profile ~/.profile 2>/dev/null
unset TMPDIR
```

<a id="mac-e-so-10"></a>

### E-SO-10 · The setup's temporary folder was deleted while it ran

- **Why:** Something deleted the setup's temporary folder (shown in brackets) in the middle of a step, usually a cleaning app or a script that empties the temporary folders. The step lost the files it had downloaded.
- **What to do:**
  - Pause the cleaning app for a few minutes and run the setup again: the steps already done are skipped.

<a id="mac-e-cfg-01"></a>

### E-CFG-01 · There are company-managed settings (managed-settings)

- **Why:** Your company installed rules for Claude Code that override yours. They can block workshop models, tools, MCP or hooks.
- **What to do:**
  - If a workshop step is blocked, show this warning to IT.
  - The file is at the path shown above. Don't change it without talking to IT.

Command (macOS):

```
cat '/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json'
```

<a id="mac-e-cfg-02"></a>

### E-CFG-02 · An ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN variable is set

- **Why:** With this variable, Claude Code uses that key instead of your login. The cost goes to the account that owns the key.
- **What to do:**
  - If the key is yours and from the Console, you can continue: the final test (step 12) checks that it works.
  - If not, remove the variable from your terminal profile (the command below shows where it is) and open a new terminal.

Command (macOS):

```
grep -n ANTHROPIC_ ~/.zshrc ~/.zprofile ~/.zshenv ~/.bash_profile ~/.bashrc ~/.profile ~/.claude/settings.json 2>/dev/null
```

<a id="mac-e-cfg-03"></a>

### E-CFG-03 · The ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL variable is set

- **Why:** With this variable, Claude Code talks to another server instead of the Anthropic API (for example, a company gateway). Prices and models may be different.
- **What to do:**
  - If IT asked you to use that gateway, you can continue.
  - If not, remove the variable (from your terminal profile or from the "env" block of ~/.claude/settings.json) and open a new terminal.

Commands (macOS):

```
grep -n ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL ~/.zshrc ~/.zprofile ~/.zshenv ~/.bash_profile ~/.claude/settings.json 2>/dev/null
unset ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
```

<a id="mac-e-cfg-04"></a>

### E-CFG-04 · Claude Code uses your company's cloud (Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry)

- **Why:** CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX or CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY is set, in the terminal or in the "env" block of a Claude Code settings file (shown above). Claude Code then uses that cloud and not the Console login. That is fine if your company set it up this way: the final test (step 12) checks that Claude answers. The workshop models (Haiku, Sonnet and Opus) must be enabled in that cloud.
- **What to do:**
  - If your company uses this cloud: nothing to do. If the final test fails, log in to the cloud in this terminal (for Bedrock: aws sso login, or AWS_PROFILE and AWS_REGION) and run the setup again.
  - If you did not mean to use it: delete the variable (the first command shows where it is) and open a new terminal. In ~/.claude/settings.json, delete it from the "env" block.
  - If the workshop models are not enabled in your company's cloud, talk to the organizer before the workshop.

Commands (macOS):

```
grep -n CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ ~/.zshrc ~/.zprofile ~/.zshenv ~/.bash_profile ~/.claude/settings.json 2>/dev/null
unset CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY
```

<a id="mac-e-cfg-05"></a>

### E-CFG-05 · The Claude Code settings.json file has an error

- **Why:** ~/.claude/settings.json is not strict JSON, or a field in it has the wrong type: the line and column, or the field, are in brackets. JSON does not allow // or /* */ comments, or a comma after the last item of a list or object (some editors' settings files do). The setup does not touch the file, so you don't lose your settings.
- **What to do:**
  - Open the file at the line and column shown and fix it: remove the comments and the comma after the last item. For a field with the wrong type, give it the shape shown in brackets.
  - Check the file with the command below (it prints JSON OK), then run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
PATH="$HOME/.workshop-claude/node/bin:$PATH" node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync(process.env.HOME + '/.claude/settings.json', 'utf8')); console.log('JSON OK')"
```

<a id="mac-e-cfg-06"></a>

### E-CFG-06 · You already had a statusline

- **Why:** Your Claude Code already shows a statusline of your own. The setup kept it and did not install the workshop one, which shows the cost.
- **What to do:**
  - You can continue: the cost also shows in /demo-cost.
  - To use the workshop statusline, run the setup again with the option below. Yours stays in the backup and comes back with --uninstall.

Command (macOS):

```
bash ~/.workshop-claude/setup-mac.sh --replace-statusline
```

<a id="mac-e-cfg-07"></a>

### E-CFG-07 · uv is not allowed to use managed Python

- **Why:** An environment variable (UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS, UV_NO_MANAGED_PYTHON or UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE) stops uv from downloading its own Python. The Agent Memory app needs that Python. The setup ignores the variable only in its own command, but other uv commands are still affected.
- **What to do:**
  - If your company set the variable, talk to IT before you change it.
  - You don't need Python installed: uv brings its own.

Command (macOS):

```
env | grep -E "^UV_(PYTHON_DOWNLOADS|NO_MANAGED_PYTHON|PYTHON_PREFERENCE)"
```

<a id="mac-e-cfg-08"></a>

### E-CFG-08 · CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is not an absolute path

- **Why:** CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (shown in brackets) is a relative path, or starts with a ~ inside quotes. Neither Claude Code nor the setup expands it, so every folder where you run claude would get its own copy of the settings, the skills and the logins (for example a folder named ~ inside the Arena). The setup stopped before changing anything.
- **What to do:**
  - Find the line with the first command. Write the path with $HOME, for example export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.claude-work" (no quotes around a ~), or delete the line if you do not need a separate Claude Code folder.
  - Open a new terminal, check the value with the second command and run the setup again.

Commands (macOS):

```
grep -n CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ~/.zshrc ~/.zprofile ~/.zshenv ~/.bash_profile ~/.profile 2>/dev/null
echo "$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR"
```

<a id="mac-e-cfg-09"></a>

### E-CFG-09 · New terminals do not use the same Claude Code folder

- **Why:** This terminal has CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so the setup put the skills, the hooks and the MCP servers in that folder (shown in brackets). A new terminal has another value, or none, so the claude you open there will not see them. This happens when the variable was exported only in this terminal, by an IDE or by direnv.
- **What to do:**
  - To keep that folder: save the variable for new terminals with the first command, open a new terminal and run the setup again.
  - To use the normal folder (~/.claude): open a new terminal where CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is not set and run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
echo "export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=\"$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR\"" >> ~/.zshrc
```

<a id="mac-e-cfg-10"></a>

### E-CFG-10 · A model override is set for Claude Code

- **Why:** A variable (shown in brackets, from the shell or from the "env" of a settings file) replaces the models Claude Code uses. That is the session model, or the sonnet, haiku and opus aliases of the workshop skills and agents. A retired model id, or one that only exists on Bedrock or Vertex, fails with a Console login, and another model changes the costs. The final test picks its own model, so it does not show this.
- **What to do:**
  - If you do not need the override, remove it: run the second command in this terminal, delete the line from ~/.zshrc and, if it is in ~/.claude/settings.json, remove it from "env". Then open a new terminal.
  - If your company set it (managed settings), talk to the organizer before the workshop.

Commands (macOS):

```
env | grep -E '^(ANTHROPIC_(MODEL|DEFAULT_[A-Z]+_MODEL|SMALL_FAST_MODEL)|CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL)='
unset ANTHROPIC_MODEL ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL
```

<a id="mac-e-cfg-11"></a>

### E-CFG-11 · Your Claude Code hooks are switched off

- **Why:** ~/.claude/settings.json has "disableAllHooks": true. Claude Code then runs no hooks and no statusline, so the workshop cost hooks and statusline don't work.
- **What to do:**
  - Remove the "disableAllHooks": true line from ~/.claude/settings.json, or set it to false.
  - Then open a new Claude session. You don't need to run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
grep -n disableAllHooks ~/.claude/settings.json
```

<a id="mac-e-perm-01"></a>

### E-PERM-01 · No permission to write to your home folder

- **Why:** The setup installs everything in your home folder, and a folder or file there (in brackets) is protected, belongs to another user (for example, it was created with sudo or by an administrator), or is a file where a folder should be.
- **What to do:**
  - Run the command the setup shows after "To fix it, run this command" (it lists exactly those paths), then run the setup again.
  - If you have no admin rights for sudo, ask IT to run it for you.
  - If a path is a file and not a folder (for example ~/.local/bin), rename it: mv ~/.local/bin ~/.local/bin.old.
  - Don't run the setup with sudo or as administrator.

Commands (macOS):

```
ls -ld ~/.local ~/.local/bin ~/.claude ~/.claude.json ~/.workshop-claude
sudo chown -R "$USER" ~/.local ~/.claude ~/.claude.json ~/.workshop-claude
```

<a id="mac-e-perm-02"></a>

### E-PERM-02 · A program was blocked by the computer's security

- **Why:** An antivirus, EDR, AppLocker, WDAC or Gatekeeper stopped a program installed in your home folder from running, or removed a file right after the download.
- **What to do:**
  - Show IT the program name from the log and ask for an exception.
  - On a Mac, if you see "cannot be opened", open System Settings > Privacy & Security and choose "Open Anyway".

Command (macOS):

```
xattr -l ~/.local/bin/claude
```

<a id="mac-e-perm-03"></a>

### E-PERM-03 · The installer asked for administrator permissions

- **Why:** An installer tried to write outside your home folder. The setup is built to work without admin.
- **What to do:**
  - Decline the elevation request and run the setup again: it uses the no-admin alternative.
  - If the problem continues, send the log to the organizer.

<a id="mac-e-git-01"></a>

### E-GIT-01 · Could not install git

- **Why:** The Mac does not have Apple's Command Line Tools, and the workshop's portable git is not working.
- **What to do:**
  - Run the setup again: the portable git is downloaded again.
  - If it still fails, install the Apple tools with the command below (it may ask for the administrator password) and run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
xcode-select --install
```

<a id="mac-e-cc-01"></a>

### E-CC-01 · The Claude Code installer failed

- **Why:** The official installer did not finish. This is usually the network (downloads.claude.ai blocked) or an antivirus blocking the file.
- **What to do:**
  - Check that you can reach claude.ai and downloads.claude.ai (code E-NET-01).
  - Run the official installer by hand and run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash -s 2.1.292
```

<a id="mac-e-cc-02"></a>

### E-CC-02 · The claude command is not in the PATH

- **Why:** Claude Code was installed in ~/.local/bin, but the terminal does not look in that folder yet.
- **What to do:**
  - Close and reopen the terminal. If it still fails, add the folder to the PATH with the command below.

Command (macOS):

```
echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
```

<a id="mac-e-cc-03"></a>

### E-CC-03 · The Claude Code version is old

- **Why:** The workshop needs Claude Code 2.1.285 or newer. There may be an old install (for example, from npm) earlier in the PATH.
- **What to do:**
  - Check which claude the terminal uses. If it is an old npm install, remove it.
  - Then run the setup again.

Commands (macOS):

```
which -a claude
npm uninstall -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```

<a id="mac-e-cc-04"></a>

### E-CC-04 · Your ~/.claude.json file has an error

- **Why:** ~/.claude.json (Claude Code's own settings, with your MCP servers) is not valid JSON, often because of a comma or quote left over from a hand edit. Claude Code would replace it with an empty file, so the setup stops here and does not touch it.
- **What to do:**
  - Fix the file shown above, or ask the organizer. The command below shows the error and where it is (open a new terminal first, so that node is found).
  - If the path shown is in ~/.claude/backups, Claude Code already replaced ~/.claude.json: your MCP servers are in that copy. Fix it and copy back what you need (for example mcpServers).
  - Then run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync(process.env.HOME + '/.claude.json', 'utf8'))"
```

<a id="mac-e-cc-05"></a>

### E-CC-05 · A new terminal runs another claude

- **Why:** A new terminal doesn't run the Claude Code the setup installed (~/.local/bin/claude). Shown above: what the terminal runs. An alias, a function or an older copy comes first, often the 2025 alias for ~/.claude/local/claude, which no longer exists.
- **What to do:**
  - Find the alias claude= line with the first command and delete it from that file.
  - Remove it from this terminal too, then open a new terminal and check that claude --version shows 2.1.285 or later.

Commands (macOS):

```
grep -ns 'alias claude=' ~/.zshrc ~/.zprofile ~/.aliases ~/.zsh_aliases ~/.bashrc ~/.bash_profile ${ZSH_CUSTOM:-$HOME/.oh-my-zsh/custom}/*.zsh
unalias claude
type -a claude
claude --version
```

<a id="mac-e-auth-01"></a>

### E-AUTH-01 · Claude Code is not logged in

- **Why:** You have not logged in yet. The workshop uses your Anthropic Console account (pay per use).
- **What to do:**
  - Run the command below. It opens the browser: sign in to the Console and authorize.
  - If you don't have an account, create one at https://platform.claude.com and add credits (Billing).
  - Then run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
claude auth login --console
```

<a id="mac-e-auth-02"></a>

### E-AUTH-02 · The login is a claude.ai subscription, not the Console

- **Why:** You are logged in with a claude.ai subscription (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise). It works, but the workshop was prepared for the Console and measures cost at API prices.
- **What to do:**
  - You can continue with the subscription: the limits are the ones of your plan.
  - To use the Console, run the command below.

Command (macOS):

```
claude auth login --console
```

<a id="mac-e-auth-03"></a>

### E-AUTH-03 · Claude Code uses another authentication method

- **Why:** The login comes from an environment variable, a token or a cloud (Bedrock or Vertex), not from the Console.
- **What to do:**
  - If this is intentional, you can continue.
  - To use the Console, remove that variable, open a new terminal and run the command below.

Commands (macOS):

```
claude auth status --text
claude auth login --console
```

<a id="mac-e-auth-04"></a>

### E-AUTH-04 · A Claude key in your environment was rejected

- **Why:** Claude Code uses the key in an environment variable (or an apiKeyHelper) instead of your Console login, and the API refused it (401: invalid, expired or revoked). Logging in again does not help while that key is set.
- **What to do:**
  - Remove the variable shown above from your terminal profile (the first command shows the file and the line) or from the "env" block of ~/.claude/settings.json.
  - In this terminal, run the second command, then run the setup again.
  - If IT gave you this key for a company gateway, ask them for a new one instead.

Commands (macOS):

```
grep -n ANTHROPIC_ ~/.zshrc ~/.zprofile ~/.zshenv ~/.bash_profile ~/.bashrc ~/.profile ~/.claude/settings.json 2>/dev/null
unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
```

<a id="mac-e-auth-05"></a>

### E-AUTH-05 · The company gateway in ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is not answering

- **Why:** ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL sends Claude Code to a company gateway (shown above) instead of api.anthropic.com, and that gateway can't be reached: VPN off, gateway down or local proxy not running. api.anthropic.com itself may be fine.
- **What to do:**
  - If you use the company gateway, connect to the VPN (or start the local proxy) and run the setup again.
  - For the workshop your Console account is enough: remove ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, if it is only for the gateway) from your terminal profile or from ~/.claude/settings.json, run the second command and run the setup again.

Commands (macOS):

```
grep -n ANTHROPIC_ ~/.zshrc ~/.zprofile ~/.zshenv ~/.bash_profile ~/.claude/settings.json 2>/dev/null
unset ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
```

<a id="mac-e-node-01"></a>

### E-NODE-01 · I couldn't install Node.js

- **Why:** The download from nodejs.org failed, or the file does not match the published SHA256SUMS.
- **What to do:**
  - Check that you can reach nodejs.org (code E-NET-01) and run the setup again.
  - Or install Node 24.22.0 (LTS) from the official site and run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://nodejs.org/dist/
```

<a id="mac-e-node-02"></a>

### E-NODE-02 · An old or broken Node comes first in the PATH

- **Why:** A new terminal finds first a Node older than 22, or one that does not start. The hooks use the new Node, but the project tests may use the old one.
- **What to do:**
  - Close and reopen the terminal, then see which node comes first with the first command below.
  - If you use nvm, select the new Node with nvm. If the first node does not start (on a Mac, often a broken Homebrew node), reinstall or remove it: brew reinstall node or brew uninstall node.
  - Check with node -v.

Commands (macOS):

```
type -a node
nvm install 22 && nvm alias default 22
node -v
```

<a id="mac-e-node-03"></a>

### E-NODE-03 · NODE_OPTIONS breaks Node in your terminal

- **Why:** NODE_OPTIONS (shown in brackets) makes every Node script fail. It is usually a --require of a file that no longer exists (VS Code or Cursor "Debug: Auto Attach", a monitoring agent) or an option this Node version rejects. The setup ran Node without it, but the workshop hooks, the statusline and the skills run Node from your terminal: the cost display and the budget warnings would not work.
- **What to do:**
  - In this terminal, run the first command. In VS Code or Cursor, run "Debug: Toggle Auto Attach" and choose Disabled or Smart, then open a new terminal.
  - If the export is in your shell profile, find it with the second command and delete it, then open a new terminal.

Commands (macOS):

```
unset NODE_OPTIONS
grep -n NODE_OPTIONS ~/.zshrc ~/.zprofile ~/.zshenv ~/.bash_profile ~/.profile 2>/dev/null
```

<a id="mac-e-uv-01"></a>

### E-UV-01 · I couldn't install uv

- **Why:** The official uv installer failed. This is usually the network (astral.sh or github.com blocked).
- **What to do:**
  - Check that you can reach astral.sh, releases.astral.sh and github.com.
  - Run the installer by hand and run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/0.13.1/install.sh | sh
```

<a id="mac-e-uv-02"></a>

### E-UV-02 · An older uv comes first in the PATH

- **Why:** The workshop needs uv 0.6.8 or newer and uses its own copy in ~/.local/bin. An older uv (for example from Homebrew or pipx) comes first in this terminal's PATH, so the uv commands you type yourself use the old one.
- **What to do:**
  - You can continue: the setup and the Agent Memory app use ~/.local/bin/uv.
  - To avoid surprises, upgrade or remove the old uv (shown above), then open a new terminal.

Commands (macOS):

```
which -a uv
brew upgrade uv
```

<a id="mac-e-uv-03"></a>

### E-UV-03 · Your uv settings file can't be read

- **Why:** uv stops because its settings file (shown above, with the line) has a syntax error. pip.conf syntax ([global], index-url = ...) is not uv.toml syntax: in uv.toml the values need quotes.
- **What to do:**
  - Fix the file, or rename it (command below), then run the setup again.
  - The Agent Memory app is optional: the skills work without it.

Command (macOS):

```
mv ~/.config/uv/uv.toml ~/.config/uv/uv.toml.bak
```

<a id="mac-e-uv-04"></a>

### E-UV-04 · The company mirror in your uv settings doesn't answer

- **Why:** Your uv settings (shown above: the file and the server) send the download of Python and of the app's packages to a company server (python-install-mirror or an index), and that server doesn't answer. It usually only answers on the VPN.
- **What to do:**
  - Connect to the VPN and run the setup again.
  - Or run the setup once without your uv settings (command below). The app is optional: the skills work without it.

Command (macOS):

```
curl -fsSL https://github.com/cx-guilherme-pinto/workshop-claude/releases/download/v1.1.0-rc.1/setup-mac.sh | UV_NO_CONFIG=1 bash
```

<a id="mac-e-gh-01"></a>

### E-GH-01 · I couldn't install GitHub CLI (gh)

- **Why:** The gh download failed or does not match the checksums file of the release.
- **What to do:**
  - Check that you can reach github.com and release-assets.githubusercontent.com.
  - Run the setup again. gh is only needed in Project 2 (real task).

Command (macOS):

```
brew install gh
```

<a id="mac-e-gh-02"></a>

### E-GH-02 · GitHub login missing (required)

- **Why:** gh is installed but has no account. The workshop needs the GitHub login for Project 2: read issues, create branches and open PRs.
- **What to do:**
  - Run the command below: it opens the browser with a code so you can confirm the login.
  - If your company uses GitHub Enterprise, replace github.com with the company server.
  - Then run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
gh auth login --hostname github.com --git-protocol https --web --scopes user:email
```

<a id="mac-e-gh-03"></a>

### E-GH-03 · GitHub did not answer

- **Why:** gh tried to check your login, but the GitHub server (shown above) did not answer in time. This usually means the company VPN is off or a proxy is blocking the connection; it is not a login problem.
- **What to do:**
  - Turn on the company VPN (or check the proxy), then run the setup again.
  - If you no longer use a server shown above, remove it from gh: gh auth logout --hostname followed by the server name.
  - The other steps were not affected. gh is only needed in Project 2 (real task).

Command (macOS):

```
gh auth status
```

<a id="mac-e-mcp-01"></a>

### E-MCP-01 · I couldn't add the Atlassian MCP

- **Why:** The claude mcp add command failed. Claude Code may be missing, or your company blocks MCP servers.
- **What to do:**
  - Run the command below by hand and read the error message.
  - If your company blocks MCP (managed-settings), use the training project with local issues.

Command (macOS):

```
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user atlassian https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp
```

<a id="mac-e-mcp-02"></a>

### E-MCP-02 · Atlassian login missing (OAuth)

- **Why:** The Jira MCP is registered, but you must log in yourself, in the browser, from inside Claude Code.
- **What to do:**
  - Open Claude Code, type /mcp, choose atlassian and follow the login.
  - If the Jira admin restricts domains, ask them to authorize Claude.

Command (macOS):

```
claude
```

<a id="mac-e-acli-01"></a>

### E-ACLI-01 · I couldn't install the Atlassian CLI (Jira backup)

- **Why:** The download from acli.atlassian.com failed, or the file does not match the expected SHA-256. acli is only used when the Jira MCP fails, so the setup continues.
- **What to do:**
  - Check that you can reach acli.atlassian.com (the company network may block it).
  - Run the setup again. Without acli, Jira still works through the MCP (/mcp).

Command (macOS):

```
curl -fsSI https://acli.atlassian.com/darwin/1.3.39-stable/acli_1.3.39-stable_darwin_arm64.tar.gz
```

<a id="mac-e-acli-02"></a>

### E-ACLI-02 · The Atlassian CLI is not logged in, or the site refused access

- **Why:** acli needs your login. Since version 1.3.15, an Atlassian site administrator must authorize the ACLI app once ("Your site admin must authorize this app…").
- **What to do:**
  - Run acli auth login and, in the terminal, choose the same site you chose in the browser.
  - If you see "site admin must authorize", ask the Jira administrator to run acli jira auth login, choose "Web" and approve the site.
  - Alternative without OAuth: create an API token at id.atlassian.com (Security > API tokens), copy it and run the command on the second line. The token goes from the clipboard to acli, without being saved in your history or in files.

Commands (macOS):

```
acli auth login
pbpaste | acli jira auth login --site <company>.atlassian.net --email <your email> --token
```

<a id="mac-e-kit-01"></a>

### E-KIT-01 · I couldn't get the workshop kit

- **Why:** The download of the kit archive failed, and the fallback git clone failed too.
- **What to do:**
  - Check that you can reach the repository server (github.com).
  - Run the setup again. If it still fails, send the log to the organizer.

Command (macOS):

```
curl -sSI https://github.com/cx-guilherme-pinto/workshop-claude/releases/download/v1.1.0-rc.1/workshop-kit-v1.1.0-rc.1.tar.gz
```

<a id="mac-e-kit-02"></a>

### E-KIT-02 · The kit archive does not match (SHA-256)

- **Why:** The downloaded file is different from the published one. It may be incomplete, or a proxy changed it.
- **What to do:**
  - Run the setup again to download it again.
  - If it happens again, stop and tell the organizer.

<a id="mac-e-kit-03"></a>

### E-KIT-03 · Installing the skills and hooks failed

- **Why:** The Node installer couldn't copy the files or update settings.json. If settings.json was already changed, its backup is in ~/.workshop-claude/backup.
- **What to do:**
  - Read the message in the log (search for "install-user").
  - Fix the cause (permissions or an invalid settings.json) and run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
ls -la ~/.claude ~/.workshop-claude/backup
```

<a id="mac-e-tel-01"></a>

### E-TEL-01 · The workshop panel can't be reached from this network

- **Why:** The panel server (shown above) did not answer from this network: a company proxy or content filter is probably blocking it. This is only a warning. The workshop works the same, and your mission book (/missions and the statusline) works without the panel. Only the workshop leaderboard won't see your progress (or your registration, if it was not done yet).
- **What to do:**
  - On the workshop day, connect to the event network or to your phone's hotspot and run the setup again: it registers you on the panel.
  - Or run the first command on that network. The second command shows whether you are registered.

Commands (macOS):

```
node ~/.workshop-claude/kit/telemetry/ctl.mjs register
node ~/.workshop-claude/kit/telemetry/ctl.mjs status
```

<a id="mac-e-tel-02"></a>

### E-TEL-02 · Your GitHub account has no verified company email

- **Why:** To appear on the workshop leaderboard, the panel checks that your GitHub account has a verified @checkmarx.com email (shown above), and this account does not. This is only a warning: you do the workshop all the same, you just do not appear on the leaderboard.
- **What to do:**
  - Add your company email to your GitHub account and confirm it (GitHub sends a link): open the page with the first command.
  - Then run the setup again (or the second command): it registers you on the panel.

Commands (macOS):

```
open https://github.com/settings/emails
node ~/.workshop-claude/kit/telemetry/ctl.mjs register
```

<a id="mac-e-tel-03"></a>

### E-TEL-03 · gh can't read your GitHub account's email

- **Why:** The workshop panel registers you with your GitHub account (through gh), and for that gh needs permission to read your account's emails (the user:email scope). gh is not logged in to github.com, or it was logged in without that permission (before the workshop asked for it). This is only a warning: gh works for Project 2 all the same; you just do not appear on the leaderboard yet.
- **What to do:**
  - Run the first command: it opens the browser so you can allow the new permission (if gh is not logged in at all, run the second one instead).
  - Then run the setup again: it registers you on the panel.

Commands (macOS):

```
gh auth refresh -h github.com -s user:email
gh auth login --hostname github.com --git-protocol https --web --scopes user:email
```

<a id="mac-e-tel-04"></a>

### E-TEL-04 · You are not registered on the workshop panel yet

- **Why:** The panel registration (with your GitHub account) has not been done on this computer yet, or it did not work the last time (network, company email or GitHub permission). This is only a warning: the workshop works the same; you just do not appear on the leaderboard.
- **What to do:**
  - Run the setup again (without --check): it registers you and says what is missing, if anything.
  - Or run the command shown above.

Command (macOS):

```
curl -fsSL https://github.com/cx-guilherme-pinto/workshop-claude/releases/download/v1.1.0-rc.1/setup-mac.sh | bash
```

<a id="mac-e-demo-01"></a>

### E-DEMO-01 · I couldn't set up the workshop projects

- **Why:** Copying the projects or running git init on them failed.
- **What to do:**
  - The reason is in brackets above, and the full message is in the log (search for "assemble").
  - Once it is fixed, run the setup again: a half-made project is rebuilt by itself, and your work is never deleted.

Command (macOS):

```
ls -la ~/workshop-claude
```

<a id="mac-e-demo-02"></a>

### E-DEMO-02 · The Arena app tests failed

- **Why:** The app's own tests (test/app.test.js) should pass from the start. The card tests are red on purpose.
- **What to do:**
  - Run the tests by hand and send the result to the organizer.
  - Check that node -v shows version 22 or higher.

Command (macOS):

```
cd ~/workshop-claude/demo-project && node --test test/app.test.js
```

<a id="mac-e-demo-03"></a>

### E-DEMO-03 · The project folder already exists and is not from the kit

- **Why:** There is already a folder with that name and with other files. The setup does not delete it.
- **What to do:**
  - Rename the folder (or delete it, if you don't need it) and run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
mv ~/workshop-claude/demo-project ~/workshop-claude/demo-project-old
```

<a id="mac-e-demo-04"></a>

### E-DEMO-04 · The Arena has its own git history: I left it as it is

- **Why:** The Arena has commits but not the arena-start tag (its starting point), so /demo-reset cannot take it back to the start. The setup never deletes your work.
- **What to do:**
  - Nothing to do if you want to keep working in this Arena.
  - To get a fresh Arena, rename this folder and run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
mv ~/workshop-claude/demo-project ~/workshop-claude/demo-project-old
```

<a id="mac-e-demo-05"></a>

### E-DEMO-05 · The Pocketknife specs and tests are not the generated ones

- **Why:** node tools/gen.mjs --check found a tool spec.md, a tool.test.js or TASKS.md that no longer matches specs/tools.json (or a specs/my-tool.json with an error). The tools themselves are only built later, by the swarm.
- **What to do:**
  - Run the check by hand: it names each file that is out of date.
  - If you changed specs/tools.json or specs/my-tool.json on purpose, run node tools/gen.mjs (without --check) to generate the files again.
  - Otherwise send the result to the organizer.

Command (macOS):

```
cd ~/workshop-claude/canivete-project && node tools/gen.mjs --check
```

<a id="mac-e-demo-06"></a>

### E-DEMO-06 · The Pocketknife has its own git history: I left it as it is

- **Why:** The Pocketknife has commits but not the canivete-start tag (its starting point), so /demo-reset cannot take it back to the start. The setup never deletes your work.
- **What to do:**
  - Nothing to do if you want to keep working in this Pocketknife.
  - To get a fresh Pocketknife, rename this folder and run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
mv ~/workshop-claude/canivete-project ~/workshop-claude/canivete-project-old
```

<a id="mac-e-mem-01"></a>

### E-MEM-01 · The Agent Memory app release is not published yet

- **Why:** I couldn't find the files for the Agent Memory app v0.5.0 on the server. The app is optional: the skills work without it.
- **What to do:**
  - You can continue. Closer to the workshop, run the setup again to install it.

<a id="mac-e-mem-02"></a>

### E-MEM-02 · The Agent Memory app file does not match (SHA-256)

- **Why:** The downloaded wheel is different from the one published in SHA256SUMS. I did not install it.
- **What to do:**
  - Run the setup again. If it happens again, tell the organizer.

<a id="mac-e-mem-03"></a>

### E-MEM-03 · Installing the Agent Memory app failed

- **Why:** uv couldn't install the app (Python 3.12 or the dependencies). This is usually the network (pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org or github.com) or the certificate of a company proxy (code E-NET-04).
- **What to do:**
  - Check that you can reach pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org.
  - Run the setup again. The app is optional: the skills work without it.

Command (macOS):

```
uv python install 3.12
```

<a id="mac-e-mem-05"></a>

### E-MEM-05 · The Agent Memory app test failed

- **Why:** The app is installed, but its self-test failed. The Python that uv installed, the note search (FTS5) or the memories folder is not working, or the search index of the notes may be damaged. The skills work without the app.
- **What to do:**
  - Run the first command below and send the result to the organizer.
  - If a line mentions the index: close Claude Code and the Agent Memory app, then run agent-memory reindex (your notes stay in Markdown).
  - Run the setup again: uv reinstalls the app and its Python.

Commands (macOS):

```
agent-memory selftest
agent-memory reindex
```

<a id="mac-e-mem-06"></a>

### E-MEM-06 · Couldn't create the Agent Memory shortcut

- **Why:** The folder for app shortcuts (in brackets) is not writable: it belongs to another user or is locked by IT. Only the shortcut is missing: the app, its window and its MCP work.
- **What to do:**
  - You can continue. Open the app window with the first command below.
  - If you want the shortcut, give the folder back to your user (or ask IT), then run the setup again.

Commands (macOS):

```
agent-memory-gui
ls -ld ~/Applications
```

<a id="mac-e-mem-07"></a>

### E-MEM-07 · The Agent Memory folder is not writable

- **Why:** The Agent Memory app is installed, but it cannot write to its memories folder (~/.agent-memory, ~/.memoria from older versions, or AGENT_MEMORY_HOME). This usually happens after a command was run with sudo, which leaves the folder owned by the administrator, or when that path is a file or a broken link. Running the setup again does not fix it. The skills work without the app.
- **What to do:**
  - Run the command the setup shows after "To fix it, run this command", then run the setup again.
  - Without admin rights: rename the folder (for example, mv ~/.agent-memory ~/.agent-memory-old), run the setup again, then copy your project folders from the old folder into the new one.
  - To see the folder and what the app reports, use the commands below.

Commands (macOS):

```
ls -ld ~/.agent-memory ~/.memoria
agent-memory selftest
```

<a id="mac-e-mem-08"></a>

### E-MEM-08 · uv is pointed at a package mirror that does not work

- **Why:** A variable (shown in brackets: UV_DEFAULT_INDEX, UV_INDEX_URL, UV_INDEX or UV_EXTRA_INDEX_URL) sends uv to a company package mirror instead of pypi.org, and that mirror did not answer or does not have the packages of the app. Often it only works on the company VPN. The skills work without the app.
- **What to do:**
  - Connect to the company VPN and run the setup again.
  - Or, if you do not need the mirror, remove the variable in this terminal (command below), delete it from your shell profile and run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
unset UV_DEFAULT_INDEX UV_INDEX_URL UV_INDEX UV_EXTRA_INDEX_URL
```

<a id="mac-e-mem-09"></a>

### E-MEM-09 · PYTHONHOME or PYTHONPATH is set in your terminal

- **Why:** Your terminal exports PYTHONHOME or PYTHONPATH (shown in brackets), often left over from an old Anaconda or conda install. They make the Python of the Agent Memory app load the wrong files and fail ("No module named encodings", ImportError). The setup and the memory MCP of Claude Code run the app without them, but agent-memory typed in your terminal fails.
- **What to do:**
  - Find the export with the command below and delete it (or the old conda block), then open a new terminal.

Command (macOS):

```
grep -nE 'PYTHONHOME|PYTHONPATH|conda' ~/.zshrc ~/.zprofile ~/.zshenv ~/.bash_profile ~/.profile 2>/dev/null
```

<a id="mac-e-mem-10"></a>

### E-MEM-10 · Your home folder path is too long for the Agent Memory app

- **Why:** The app keeps its search index in <memories folder>/.index/index-v3.sqlite, and the SQLite of its Python only opens database paths of up to 504 bytes (in brackets, the length here). With a very long home folder path the index never opens: running the setup again or agent-memory reindex does not fix it. Your notes are safe, and the skills work without the app.
- **What to do:**
  - Put the memories in a shorter folder: add the line below to ~/.zshrc, open a new terminal and run the setup again. The notes you already have stay in the old folder: copy them over if you want them.

Command (macOS):

```
echo 'export AGENT_MEMORY_HOME="/Users/Shared/agent-memory-$USER"' >> ~/.zshrc
```

<a id="mac-e-mem-11"></a>

### E-MEM-11 · Another folder has memories that the Agent Memory app does not show

- **Why:** The app reads one data folder: AGENT_MEMORY_HOME, else MEMORIA_HOME, else ~/.memoria (from older versions) while ~/.agent-memory has no notes, else ~/.agent-memory. Another folder (in brackets, with how many notes it has) also has notes, usually left over from an older version or from a variable set in another terminal. Nothing was moved or deleted, and the app, its MCP and the skills work.
- **What to do:**
  - You can continue. The first command shows the folder in use (the line "Memory folder") and the other folder.
  - To see those notes, move their project folders into the folder in use. Or point AGENT_MEMORY_HOME to the folder you want in your shell profile (Windows: in your user variables), open a new terminal and run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
agent-memory selftest
```

<a id="mac-e-desk-01"></a>

### E-DESK-01 · Claude Desktop has limits with the Console

- **Why:** Claude Desktop only signs in with a claude.ai account, and the Code tab needs a subscription. All the workshop hands-on work runs in Claude Code (terminal).
- **What to do:**
  - You don't need to do anything. Desktop is optional.

<a id="mac-e-desk-02"></a>

### E-DESK-02 · I couldn't install Claude Desktop

- **Why:** The Claude Desktop download or install failed. It is optional.
- **What to do:**
  - If you want it, download it by hand from https://claude.ai/download.

<a id="mac-e-prof-01"></a>

### E-PROF-01 · The setup could not add the workshop folders to a shell profile

- **Why:** New terminals read this file when they start, but the setup could not read or change it. It is read-only, belongs to another user (for example, it was created with sudo), or links to a file that is missing or read-only (dotfiles, iCloud). The setup left it as it was.
- **What to do:**
  - Add the first line below at the end of the file the setup named (or of the file it links to in your dotfiles), then open a new terminal.
  - If the file is not read-only on purpose, check it with the second command, make it readable and writable for you (or ask whoever manages your Mac), and run the setup again.

Commands (macOS):

```
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.workshop-claude/bin:$HOME/.workshop-claude/node/bin:$PATH"
ls -lO ~/.zshrc
```

<a id="mac-e-prof-02"></a>

### E-PROF-02 · A shell profile has an incomplete workshop block

- **Why:** The file has a '# >>> workshop-claude >>>' line without its '# <<< workshop-claude <<<' line, or the other way round (an old or hand-edited block). The setup did not change the file, so none of your lines were lost.
- **What to do:**
  - Open the file the setup named and delete the old workshop lines: the marker line and the PATH lines that follow it. Keep your own lines.
  - Then run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
grep -n workshop-claude ~/.zshrc
```

<a id="mac-e-smoke-01"></a>

### E-SMOKE-01 · The final Claude test failed

- **Why:** Claude Code couldn't answer a simple request. It may be the login, the network or credits.
- **What to do:**
  - Run the command below and read the error message.
  - Check the login (code E-AUTH-01) and the credits (code E-SMOKE-02).

Command (macOS):

```
claude -p "Reply in English with only the word OK" --model claude-haiku-5-5
```

<a id="mac-e-smoke-02"></a>

### E-SMOKE-02 · The Console account has no credits

- **Why:** The API refused the request because the balance is too low (credit balance too low).
- **What to do:**
  - Open https://platform.claude.com, go to Billing and add credits (recommended: a limit well above US$ 10).
  - Then run the setup again.

<a id="mac-e-smoke-03"></a>

### E-SMOKE-03 · Request limit reached (error 429)

- **Why:** The API is limiting the requests from your organization. New accounts have lower limits.
- **What to do:**
  - Wait a minute and run the setup again.

<a id="mac-e-smoke-04"></a>

### E-SMOKE-04 · The test model is not available in your account

- **Why:** Your organization has no access to the claude-haiku-5-5 model, or a company gateway blocks it.
- **What to do:**
  - Check the available models in the Console and talk to the organizer.

<a id="mac-e-smoke-05"></a>

### E-SMOKE-05 · One of your hooks blocked the test request

- **Why:** A hook in your Claude Code settings (~/.claude/settings.json, or one your company manages) blocked the request before it reached Claude. Shown above: the event (usually UserPromptSubmit) and the hook's reason. Every prompt in the workshop would be blocked the same way.
- **What to do:**
  - Do what the hook's message asks, or ask whoever set up that hook to let the workshop prompts through.
  - Or remove that hook from ~/.claude/settings.json for the workshop (the command below shows it), then run the setup again.

Command (macOS):

```
grep -n -A12 '"hooks"' ~/.claude/settings.json
```

<a id="mac-e-smoke-06"></a>

### E-SMOKE-06 · One of your hooks makes Claude wait

- **Why:** With your hooks (shown above: the events and the file), Claude didn't answer in time. Without them it answered, so the login and the network are fine. A hook such as SessionStart is waiting for something, often a server that only answers on the VPN, and every Claude session in the workshop would wait for it too.
- **What to do:**
  - Connect to the VPN if the hook needs it, or give that hook a short "timeout" (in seconds).
  - Or remove that hook from ~/.claude/settings.json for the workshop (the first command shows it), then run the setup again.
  - The second command checks Claude without your hooks.

Commands (macOS):

```
grep -n -A12 '"hooks"' ~/.claude/settings.json
claude -p "Reply in English with only the word OK" --model claude-haiku-5-5 --settings '{"disableAllHooks":true}'
```

<a id="mac-e-git-04"></a>

### E-GIT-04 · The portable git download is corrupted

- **Why:** The downloaded file does not have the expected SHA-256. A proxy may be changing the download.
- **What to do:**
  - Run the setup again.
  - If it still fails, try another network and show setup.log to whoever is helping you.

Command (macOS):

```
xcode-select --install
```

## Windows

<a id="windows-e-setup-01"></a>

### E-SETUP-01 · This step is not done yet

- **Why:** The setup has not installed this on this computer yet, or the install stopped halfway.
- **What to do:**
  - Run the full setup, without --check. Steps already done are skipped.

Command (Windows):

```
irm https://github.com/cx-guilherme-pinto/workshop-claude/releases/download/v1.1.0-rc.1/bootstrap-windows.ps1 | iex
```

<a id="windows-e-net-01"></a>

### E-NET-01 · A required domain is blocked

- **Why:** The network does not let you reach one or more domains that the workshop needs. This is usually a company firewall or filter.
- **What to do:**
  - Ask your IT team to allow the domains listed in docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md (section "Required domains").
  - Or use another network (for example, your phone's hotspot) and run the setup again.

Command (Windows):

```
Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Method Head https://api.anthropic.com
```

<a id="windows-e-net-02"></a>

### E-NET-02 · The server name does not resolve (DNS)

- **Why:** The computer can't translate the domain name into an address. The network may require a VPN, or DNS is failing.
- **What to do:**
  - Connect to the company VPN if you use one, or disconnect it if it is blocking.
  - Try another network and run the setup again.

Command (Windows):

```
Resolve-DnsName api.anthropic.com
```

<a id="windows-e-net-03"></a>

### E-NET-03 · The proxy does not answer or refuses the request

- **Why:** Your terminal sends the traffic through a proxy (HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY or the system proxy). That proxy does not answer, its name does not resolve, or it refused the request (for example, error 407: it asks for a username and password). A proxy left over from the office network or from an old VPN causes this.
- **What to do:**
  - If you are not on the office network or VPN, remove the proxy from this terminal (first command below) and delete the line that sets it in ~/.zshrc or ~/.zprofile. If it is the system proxy, turn it off in System Settings > Network > Details > Proxies. Then run the setup again.
  - On Windows, the second command removes the proxy from your user environment variables, and the system proxy is in Settings > Network & internet > Proxy.
  - If the company network needs the proxy, connect the VPN, or set the right proxy for this session and run the setup again.
  - If the proxy asks for a username and password (error 407), ask IT for a proxy without authentication or an exception for the workshop domains.
  - On Windows, if even the first command of the setup gets error 407, run it with the last command: it sends your Windows login to the proxy.

Commands (Windows):

```
Remove-Item Env:HTTPS_PROXY, Env:HTTP_PROXY, Env:ALL_PROXY -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('HTTPS_PROXY', $null, 'User')
$env:HTTPS_PROXY = 'http://proxy.company:8080'
$env:NO_PROXY = 'localhost,127.0.0.1'
[Net.WebRequest]::DefaultWebProxy.Credentials = [Net.CredentialCache]::DefaultNetworkCredentials; irm https://github.com/cx-guilherme-pinto/workshop-claude/releases/download/v1.1.0-rc.1/bootstrap-windows.ps1 | iex
```

<a id="windows-e-net-04"></a>

### E-NET-04 · Your company intercepts HTTPS traffic (its own certificate)

- **Why:** A site the setup needs (api.anthropic.com, github.com or pypi.org) shows a certificate that does not come from a public authority: the company network opens the traffic and encrypts it again. The setup exports the company certificates from the system to ~/.workshop-claude/ca-company.pem, adds your ~/.workshop-claude/ca.pem if you have one, and configures Claude Code to use them and uv to use the system certificates.
- **What to do:**
  - Usually you don't need to do anything: the setup already set NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS and UV_SYSTEM_CERTS.
  - If the final test or the Agent Memory app still fails with a certificate error, ask IT for the company root certificate in PEM format and save it as ~/.workshop-claude/ca.pem (the setup never overwrites that file). Then run the setup again.

Command (Windows):

```
Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\Root, Cert:\CurrentUser\Root | Select-Object Subject, Issuer
```

<a id="windows-e-net-05"></a>

### E-NET-05 · No connection to the Anthropic API

- **Why:** Claude Code can't talk to api.anthropic.com. Without this there is no workshop, and Claude can't help you diagnose the problem either.
- **What to do:**
  - Check that you can open https://api.anthropic.com in the browser (a JSON error page means you can reach it).
  - If your network needs a proxy, set HTTPS_PROXY before you run the setup. If a proxy is already set, see E-NET-03 and E-NET-08.
  - Ask IT to allow api.anthropic.com, claude.ai and platform.claude.com.

Command (Windows):

```
Test-NetConnection api.anthropic.com -Port 443
```

<a id="windows-e-net-06"></a>

### E-NET-06 · Proxy with NTLM or Kerberos authentication only

- **Why:** Claude Code and Node can't authenticate to NTLM or Kerberos proxies. This type of proxy is not supported.
- **What to do:**
  - Ask IT for a proxy exception for the workshop domains.
  - Or use another network (your phone's hotspot) during the workshop.

<a id="windows-e-net-07"></a>

### E-NET-07 · The download failed

- **Why:** A file was not downloaded, or it arrived incomplete (the transfer stopped in the middle). This is usually a short network failure or a crowded WiFi.
- **What to do:**
  - Run the setup again. Steps already done are skipped.
  - If it always fails on the same file, try another network (for example, your phone's hotspot) and check the proxy (codes E-NET-01 and E-NET-03).

Command (Windows):

```
irm https://github.com/cx-guilherme-pinto/workshop-claude/releases/download/v1.1.0-rc.1/bootstrap-windows.ps1 | iex
```

<a id="windows-e-net-08"></a>

### E-NET-08 · Claude Code is set to use a proxy that does not answer on this network

- **Why:** The "env" block of ~/.claude/settings.json has HTTPS_PROXY, and Claude Code uses it even when your terminal has no proxy. That proxy does not answer here. It is usually a proxy the setup saved on another network (for example, the office proxy).
- **What to do:**
  - Run the setup again on this network: it removes or updates the proxy it saved.
  - If you added this proxy yourself, delete the HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY lines from the "env" block of ~/.claude/settings.json.
  - Back on the office network, run the setup again to put the proxy back.

Commands (Windows):

```
irm https://github.com/cx-guilherme-pinto/workshop-claude/releases/download/v1.1.0-rc.1/bootstrap-windows.ps1 | iex
Select-String -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\settings.json" -Pattern proxy
```

<a id="windows-e-net-09"></a>

### E-NET-09 · A certificate variable points to a missing or wrong file

- **Why:** SSL_CERT_FILE, CURL_CA_BUNDLE, GIT_SSL_CAINFO, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or SSL_CERT_DIR (shown in brackets), or a cacert line in ~/.curlrc, points to a certificate file that does not exist or does not have the right certificates. It is often left over from an old Homebrew, Anaconda or Zscaler install. curl then fails on every site with "curl: (77) error setting certificate verify locations", and uv fails with "invalid peer certificate". The setup ignores the variable in its own commands, but your terminal still has it.
- **What to do:**
  - If the install command itself stops with curl: (77), run the first command below in the same terminal and paste the install command again.
  - Find the export in your shell profile with the second command, delete that line (or point it to the right file) and open a new terminal.

Commands (Windows):

```
Get-ChildItem Env: | Where-Object Name -match 'SSL_CERT|CA_BUNDLE|CAINFO|EXTRA_CA_CERTS'
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('SSL_CERT_FILE', $null, 'User')
```

<a id="windows-e-net-10"></a>

### E-NET-10 · uv doesn't trust your company's certificate

- **Why:** Downloading the app's Python (github.com) or its packages (pypi.org) failed with a certificate error, even with the system certificates (UV_SYSTEM_CERTS) and with ~/.workshop-claude/ca.pem if you have one. Your company's root certificate is not among them.
- **What to do:**
  - Ask IT for the company root certificate in PEM format and save it as ~/.workshop-claude/ca.pem. The setup never overwrites that file.
  - Then run the setup again: it gives that certificate to uv. The commands below do the same by hand. The app is optional: the skills work without it.

Commands (Windows):

```
$env:SSL_CERT_FILE = "$env:USERPROFILE\.workshop-claude\ca-bundle-uv.pem"
uv python install 3.12
```

<a id="windows-e-so-01"></a>

### E-SO-01 · Windows older than 10.0.18362 (version 1903)

- **Why:** This Windows version is old. winget and Claude Desktop don't work on it, and other things may fail.
- **What to do:**
  - Update Windows with Windows Update, or ask IT.
  - The setup continues, but uses direct installers instead of winget.

Command (Windows):

```
winver
```

<a id="windows-e-so-02"></a>

### E-SO-02 · Windows on ARM64

- **Why:** The computer has an ARM processor. The setup picks the ARM64 versions of Node, gh and Git when they exist.
- **What to do:**
  - You don't need to do anything. If a step fails, tell the organizer and give them the code of this warning.

<a id="windows-e-so-03"></a>

### E-SO-03 · Your home folder is in OneDrive

- **Why:** Your home folder, or the folder of the workshop projects, is synced by OneDrive. Syncing can lock files while the agents are working.
- **What to do:**
  - During the workshop, pause OneDrive syncing (OneDrive icon > Pause syncing).
  - The projects are in ~/workshop-claude. If that folder is inside OneDrive, move it out.

<a id="windows-e-so-05"></a>

### E-SO-05 · PowerShell in restricted mode

- **Why:** PowerShell is in ConstrainedLanguage mode, because of a company policy (AppLocker or WDAC). In this mode the setup can't run.
- **What to do:**
  - Ask IT for an exception for the workshop setup, or do the setup on another computer.
  - Check the mode with the command below: it must say FullLanguage.

Command (Windows):

```
$ExecutionContext.SessionState.LanguageMode
```

<a id="windows-e-so-06"></a>

### E-SO-06 · Low disk space

- **Why:** There are less than 3 GB free in your home folder. The tools and the projects need about 2 GB.
- **What to do:**
  - Free up space (for example, empty the Downloads folder) and run the setup again.

Command (Windows):

```
Get-PSDrive C
```

<a id="windows-e-so-07"></a>

### E-SO-07 · A company policy blocks PowerShell scripts

- **Why:** Group Policy sets the PowerShell execution policy, and it wins over "-ExecutionPolicy Bypass". With AllSigned or Restricted, no unsigned script can run: not the setup, and not the official installers of Claude Code and uv.
- **What to do:**
  - Ask IT for an exception for the workshop (scripts from your user folder), or do the setup on another computer.
  - If the policy is RemoteSigned and you downloaded setup-windows.ps1 with the browser, unblock the file first (second command) and run it again.

Commands (Windows):

```
Get-ExecutionPolicy -List
Unblock-File -LiteralPath .\setup-windows.ps1
```

<a id="windows-e-so-08"></a>

### E-SO-08 · PowerShell ISE can't run the setup

- **Why:** PowerShell ISE has no real console: the programs that ask you something (the Claude Code, GitHub and Jira logins) would wait forever.
- **What to do:**
  - Open "Windows PowerShell" from the Start menu (not "Windows PowerShell ISE") and run the setup command there.

Command (Windows):

```
irm https://github.com/cx-guilherme-pinto/workshop-claude/releases/download/v1.1.0-rc.1/bootstrap-windows.ps1 | iex
```

<a id="windows-e-so-09"></a>

### E-SO-09 · The temporary folder variable points to a folder that cannot be used

- **Why:** TMPDIR (on Windows, TEMP or TMP), shown in brackets, points to a folder that does not exist or cannot be written, often an export copied from another computer. The setup used another temporary folder, but other programs in your terminal (Claude Code, uv, npm) may fail.
- **What to do:**
  - Find the export with the first command and delete it (macOS sets TMPDIR by itself), then open a new terminal.

Command (Windows):

```
[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('TEMP', 'User'); [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('TMP', 'User')
```

<a id="windows-e-so-10"></a>

### E-SO-10 · The setup's temporary folder was deleted while it ran

- **Why:** Something deleted the setup's temporary folder (shown in brackets) in the middle of a step, usually a cleaning app or a script that empties the temporary folders. The step lost the files it had downloaded.
- **What to do:**
  - Pause the cleaning app for a few minutes and run the setup again: the steps already done are skipped.

<a id="windows-e-cfg-01"></a>

### E-CFG-01 · There are company-managed settings (managed-settings)

- **Why:** Your company installed rules for Claude Code that override yours. They can block workshop models, tools, MCP or hooks.
- **What to do:**
  - If a workshop step is blocked, show this warning to IT.
  - The file is at the path shown above. Don't change it without talking to IT.

Command (Windows):

```
Get-Content "$env:ProgramFiles\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json"
```

<a id="windows-e-cfg-02"></a>

### E-CFG-02 · An ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN variable is set

- **Why:** With this variable, Claude Code uses that key instead of your login. The cost goes to the account that owns the key.
- **What to do:**
  - If the key is yours and from the Console, you can continue: the final test (step 12) checks that it works.
  - If not, remove the variable from your terminal profile (the command below shows where it is) and open a new terminal.

Commands (Windows):

```
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY', $null, 'User')
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN', $null, 'User')
```

<a id="windows-e-cfg-03"></a>

### E-CFG-03 · The ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL variable is set

- **Why:** With this variable, Claude Code talks to another server instead of the Anthropic API (for example, a company gateway). Prices and models may be different.
- **What to do:**
  - If IT asked you to use that gateway, you can continue.
  - If not, remove the variable (from your terminal profile or from the "env" block of ~/.claude/settings.json) and open a new terminal.

Command (Windows):

```
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL', $null, 'User')
```

<a id="windows-e-cfg-04"></a>

### E-CFG-04 · Claude Code uses your company's cloud (Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry)

- **Why:** CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX or CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY is set, in the terminal or in the "env" block of a Claude Code settings file (shown above). Claude Code then uses that cloud and not the Console login. That is fine if your company set it up this way: the final test (step 12) checks that Claude answers. The workshop models (Haiku, Sonnet and Opus) must be enabled in that cloud.
- **What to do:**
  - If your company uses this cloud: nothing to do. If the final test fails, log in to the cloud in this terminal (for Bedrock: aws sso login, or AWS_PROFILE and AWS_REGION) and run the setup again.
  - If you did not mean to use it: delete the variable (the first command shows where it is) and open a new terminal. In ~/.claude/settings.json, delete it from the "env" block.
  - If the workshop models are not enabled in your company's cloud, talk to the organizer before the workshop.

Commands (Windows):

```
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK', $null, 'User')
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX', $null, 'User')
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY', $null, 'User')
Select-String -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\settings.json" -Pattern CLAUDE_CODE_USE_
```

<a id="windows-e-cfg-05"></a>

### E-CFG-05 · The Claude Code settings.json file has an error

- **Why:** ~/.claude/settings.json is not strict JSON, or a field in it has the wrong type: the line and column, or the field, are in brackets. JSON does not allow // or /* */ comments, or a comma after the last item of a list or object (some editors' settings files do). The setup does not touch the file, so you don't lose your settings.
- **What to do:**
  - Open the file at the line and column shown and fix it: remove the comments and the comma after the last item. For a field with the wrong type, give it the shape shown in brackets.
  - Check the file with the command below (it prints JSON OK), then run the setup again.

Command (Windows):

```
node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync(process.env.USERPROFILE + '/.claude/settings.json', 'utf8')); console.log('JSON OK')"
```

<a id="windows-e-cfg-06"></a>

### E-CFG-06 · You already had a statusline

- **Why:** Your Claude Code already shows a statusline of your own. The setup kept it and did not install the workshop one, which shows the cost.
- **What to do:**
  - You can continue: the cost also shows in /demo-cost.
  - To use the workshop statusline, run the setup again with the option below. Yours stays in the backup and comes back with --uninstall.

Command (Windows):

```
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$env:USERPROFILE\.workshop-claude\setup-windows.ps1" -ReplaceStatusline
```

<a id="windows-e-cfg-07"></a>

### E-CFG-07 · uv is not allowed to use managed Python

- **Why:** An environment variable (UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS, UV_NO_MANAGED_PYTHON or UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE) stops uv from downloading its own Python. The Agent Memory app needs that Python. The setup ignores the variable only in its own command, but other uv commands are still affected.
- **What to do:**
  - If your company set the variable, talk to IT before you change it.
  - You don't need Python installed: uv brings its own.

Command (Windows):

```
Get-ChildItem Env:UV_*
```

<a id="windows-e-cfg-08"></a>

### E-CFG-08 · CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is not an absolute path

- **Why:** CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (shown in brackets) is a relative path, or starts with a ~ inside quotes. Neither Claude Code nor the setup expands it, so every folder where you run claude would get its own copy of the settings, the skills and the logins (for example a folder named ~ inside the Arena). The setup stopped before changing anything.
- **What to do:**
  - Find the line with the first command. Write the path with $HOME, for example export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.claude-work" (no quotes around a ~), or delete the line if you do not need a separate Claude Code folder.
  - Open a new terminal, check the value with the second command and run the setup again.

Commands (Windows):

```
[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR', 'User')
Remove-Item Env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
```

<a id="windows-e-cfg-09"></a>

### E-CFG-09 · New terminals do not use the same Claude Code folder

- **Why:** This terminal has CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so the setup put the skills, the hooks and the MCP servers in that folder (shown in brackets). A new terminal has another value, or none, so the claude you open there will not see them. This happens when the variable was exported only in this terminal, by an IDE or by direnv.
- **What to do:**
  - To keep that folder: save the variable for new terminals with the first command, open a new terminal and run the setup again.
  - To use the normal folder (~/.claude): open a new terminal where CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is not set and run the setup again.

Command (Windows):

```
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR', $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, 'User')
```

<a id="windows-e-cfg-10"></a>

### E-CFG-10 · A model override is set for Claude Code

- **Why:** A variable (shown in brackets, from the shell or from the "env" of a settings file) replaces the models Claude Code uses. That is the session model, or the sonnet, haiku and opus aliases of the workshop skills and agents. A retired model id, or one that only exists on Bedrock or Vertex, fails with a Console login, and another model changes the costs. The final test picks its own model, so it does not show this.
- **What to do:**
  - If you do not need the override, remove it: run the second command in this terminal, delete the line from ~/.zshrc and, if it is in ~/.claude/settings.json, remove it from "env". Then open a new terminal.
  - If your company set it (managed settings), talk to the organizer before the workshop.

Command (Windows):

```
Get-ChildItem Env: | Where-Object Name -match 'ANTHROPIC_.*MODEL|CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL'
```

<a id="windows-e-cfg-11"></a>

### E-CFG-11 · Your Claude Code hooks are switched off

- **Why:** ~/.claude/settings.json has "disableAllHooks": true. Claude Code then runs no hooks and no statusline, so the workshop cost hooks and statusline don't work.
- **What to do:**
  - Remove the "disableAllHooks": true line from ~/.claude/settings.json, or set it to false.
  - Then open a new Claude session. You don't need to run the setup again.

Command (Windows):

```
Select-String -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\settings.json" -Pattern disableAllHooks
```

<a id="windows-e-perm-01"></a>

### E-PERM-01 · No permission to write to your home folder

- **Why:** The setup installs everything in your home folder, and a folder or file there (in brackets) is protected, belongs to another user (for example, it was created with sudo or by an administrator), or is a file where a folder should be.
- **What to do:**
  - Run the command the setup shows after "To fix it, run this command" (it lists exactly those paths), then run the setup again.
  - If you have no admin rights for sudo, ask IT to run it for you.
  - If a path is a file and not a folder (for example ~/.local/bin), rename it: mv ~/.local/bin ~/.local/bin.old.
  - Don't run the setup with sudo or as administrator.

Commands (Windows):

```
icacls "$env:USERPROFILE\.workshop-claude"
icacls "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude"
icacls "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude.json"
icacls "$env:USERPROFILE\.local\bin"
```

<a id="windows-e-perm-02"></a>

### E-PERM-02 · A program was blocked by the computer's security

- **Why:** An antivirus, EDR, AppLocker, WDAC or Gatekeeper stopped a program installed in your home folder from running, or removed a file right after the download.
- **What to do:**
  - Show IT the program name from the log and ask for an exception.
  - On a Mac, if you see "cannot be opened", open System Settings > Privacy & Security and choose "Open Anyway".

Command (Windows):

```
Get-MpThreatDetection | Select-Object -First 5
```

<a id="windows-e-perm-03"></a>

### E-PERM-03 · The installer asked for administrator permissions

- **Why:** An installer tried to write outside your home folder. The setup is built to work without admin.
- **What to do:**
  - Decline the elevation request and run the setup again: it uses the no-admin alternative.
  - If the problem continues, send the log to the organizer.

<a id="windows-e-git-02"></a>

### E-GIT-02 · I couldn't install Git for Windows

- **Why:** winget is not available or failed, and the direct Git installer also failed.
- **What to do:**
  - Install Git for Windows by hand, choosing "Only for me" (no admin), and run the setup again.
  - If your company has a software portal (Company Portal, Software Center), install Git from there.

Command (Windows):

```
winget install --id Git.Git -e --scope user --source winget
```

<a id="windows-e-git-03"></a>

### E-GIT-03 · I couldn't find Git Bash (bash.exe)

- **Why:** On Windows, Claude Code uses Git Bash to run commands and hooks. git is there, but I couldn't find bash.exe next to it or in the usual Git for Windows folders.
- **What to do:**
  - Reinstall Git for Windows (it includes Git Bash) and run the setup again.
  - If bash.exe is in another folder, set the variable below to the right path.

Command (Windows):

```
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH', 'C:\path\to\Git\bin\bash.exe', 'User')
```

<a id="windows-e-cc-01"></a>

### E-CC-01 · The Claude Code installer failed

- **Why:** The official installer did not finish. This is usually the network (downloads.claude.ai blocked) or an antivirus blocking the file.
- **What to do:**
  - Check that you can reach claude.ai and downloads.claude.ai (code E-NET-01).
  - Run the official installer by hand and run the setup again.

Command (Windows):

```
& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1))) 2.1.292
```

<a id="windows-e-cc-02"></a>

### E-CC-02 · The claude command is not in the PATH

- **Why:** Claude Code was installed in ~/.local/bin, but the terminal does not look in that folder yet.
- **What to do:**
